cells.tense: You are standing where a great deal of feeling is arriving at once, and you can tell it apart.
cells.ask: Say out loud which one pull is yours today and let the rest stay on the table. Then give the chosen one an hour before you decide anything else.
cells.core:
A lot is arriving at once right now — faces, offers, possibilities, the whole spread of what could be felt. And you're reading it, not drowning in it. You can name what's pulling you, why it pulls, and hold that without needing to settle on it yet. Nothing is lost by waiting a beat on it.

What keeps this steady is that you're looking at the pattern instead of obeying the first strong pull. You feel the pull, you see the shape it makes, and you move from there. That's the balance, and it isn't holding back. Keep reading what's in front of you, name the one that's yours, and pick from what you can actually see.
cells.sheetLine: A lot is pulling. You're reading the pattern, not obeying it.

cells.tense: You are already living in a future where one of these pulls has to win, and it hasn't happened yet.
cells.ask: Name the two pulls you keep comparing, pick one for this week, and write down what you'll leave alone until the week is out.
cells.core:
Before anything's decided, you're bracing — sizing up which pull will win, what it'll cost, who gets left out. That pressing is costing you contact with what's actually here. Held well, the pulls sit side by side for a while, each one felt and named, none of them sorted yet. Not indecision — the whole harvest arriving at once before anything narrows it.

What you're doing instead is spending on a decision that's still forming. All that watching for the outcome is a tax you're paying early, and it's coming out of the thing you're trying to choose between. Pick one for this week and let the others keep their place. What you leave alone isn't gone. It's real, it's waiting, and it's still yours to come back to.

cells.tense: You were standing at a threshold when the pull stopped reaching you the way it used to.
cells.ask: Pick one thing in front of you this week and stay near it for ten minutes — just notice what it puts in you, no verdict and no decision after.
cells.core:
Pull isn't arriving the way it used to. Plenty of things out there could move you, but they land flat, and you can tell by comparison — you remember a warmer response in yourself than the one you're having now. Nothing here needs an explanation from you. That's only the temperature.

Held well, something small gets met and moves you a little, and you let it, without insisting it mean anything. What's absent isn't the pull. It's the meeting — letting one thing reach you before you know what you'll do with it. One thing this week, ten minutes near it, and nothing decided afterward. That's the whole ask.
cells.sheetLine: The pull still shows up. It's the meeting it isn't getting.

cells.tense: You are already the one gathering what people feel, and you talk about it like it's happening on its own.
cells.ask: Catch one thing you notice about a person today, say it out loud to them, and when it lands, mark that you chose to say it. Do the same once more before the week ends.
cells.core:
You walk into a room and things shift — you feel what's in the air, who needs what, what could be said. And you call it the room, or the mood, or just reading people. It isn't that. You're doing it, and you've been doing it so long it stopped having your name on it.

Held well, it's deliberate: you see something, you say it, and you know the call was yours. Being discreet is fine — what slid out of place isn't the act, it's who it belongs to. Say one thing to one person, and the marker goes back where it goes. You don't have to claim a temperament. Claim the one move.
cells.sheetLine: The gathering is yours. You've been calling it the room.
